spots.cost: Free. Cabo da Roca (mainland Europe’s westernmost point) has free parking and viewpoints; Praia da Ursa is a steep unofficial scramble (not for little kids alone); Azenhas do Mar has a natural sea pool below the village.
spots.climate: June: sunny but windy and Atlantic-cold water. Great for views and tide pools, not long swims — that is what Sicily is for.
spots.saveHtml: Save Pack a picnic — there is little food at Cabo da Roca beyond one café, and the views beat overpriced snacks.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge A cliffside lunch or sunset drink at Azenhas do Mar, or a short Sintra-coast e-bike stretch.
spots.restoHtml:

          <p class="book"><b>Book:</b> Apartment-hotel or family room with AC near Cascais/Estoril train access. Current July 2026 proxy data shows Cascais places averaging around $157/night overall, with stronger family/coastal options commonly $200-$320/night.</p>

Booking Rules

What can break the plan

  • The Mon Jun 14 LIS-PMO hop is the hinge. Current route data shows the nonstop, but 2027 schedules must be confirmed before locking nonrefundable Sicily lodging.
  • Keep the airfare gate hard. This itinerary is designed for $12k target / $15k cap, not business-class comfort.
  • Hold refundable lodging first. Sicily family apartments with AC and parking are scarce once July-style demand arrives.

Driving Sicily

How to keep it sane

  • One car, west to east. Pick up near Palermo, drop at Catania, and never drive back to Palermo.
  • ZTLs matter. Cefalù and Taormina can punish casual driving; lodging must spell out parking.
  • Do not overload transfer days. Cefalù to the Taormina coast is one easy hop — no need to add Agrigento.

Tickets

Timed entries and paid anchors

  • Pena Palace is timed-entry. Only add it if a good early slot exists; otherwise Regaleira is the better family stop.
  • Regaleira has clear pricing. In 2026 it is EUR15 adult and EUR10 per youth 6-17, so a family of four is about EUR50 (there is no combined family ticket).
  • Etna is weather-dependent. Free craters first; cable car only if visibility and volcanic conditions justify it.

Picky Eaters

Plain food at every base

  • Cascais/Sintra. Pizza, pasta, pastries, sandwiches, and simple grills are easy.
  • Cefalù/Palermo. Pizza, pasta counters, arancini, burgers/fries, and gelato keep dinner low-friction.
  • Taormina/Giardini. Choose pizzerias and beach-town spots for kids; save seafood-heavy places for adult lunches.

Heat + Water

The real trip rhythm

  • Sightsee early or late. Palermo, Taormina, and Etna are better before the worst afternoon heat.
  • Sicily solves most of the water issue. June is not August bathwater, but it is materially warmer than Portugal's Atlantic.
  • Protect the final swim day. Do not turn Jun 20 into another logistics day.

What People Are Saying

Insider notes from people who've actually gone

Crowd-sourced from Reddit, TripAdvisor forums, and local-run blogs (July 2026) — the off-the-beaten-path stuff guidebooks skip. Reconfirm access rules, tides, and prices closer to travel.

Sicily's crowd clock

Same spots, half the people

  • Cefalù beach by 7–8am. The free sand at either end fills first; after 10am in summer it's "Tetris with sweaty strangers," and the lidos want €30+. Hike La Rocca before 9:30 — little shade, not for kids under ~6.
  • Time Taormina around the cruise ships. They dock ~9:30am and the town chokes 11am–4pm; do Corso Umberto and the Greek Theatre before 9:30 or after 5pm. Check the day's dock schedule on cruisemapper.com.
  • Isola Bella is a free beach. No island admission; walk the sandbar only at low tide (or you're stranded), bring water shoes for the scalding pebbles, and watch for mauve-stinger jellyfish in June.

Etna with kids, done right

Don't force the summit

  • Etna Sud + the lower Silvestri craters is plenty. Take the Rifugio Sapienza cable car; the walkable lower craters (~2000m) deliver the moonscape without altitude sickness or a death march. Guides are legally required above 2500m.
  • Add a lava tube. A guided volcanic cave (e.g. Grotta dei Ladroni on the quieter Etna Nord side, helmet + torch) is a hit with kids — verify the age minimum with the operator first.
  • Late spring / early summer wins. Peak summer can see 50,000 visitors a day; early June is far calmer and the lava fields are snow-free and visible.

ZTL: the fine that shows up 18 months later

The hidden car-rental trap

  • One wrong turn into a ZTL = €50–320, mailed months later — plus a rental-company admin fee on top, and multiple cameras can stack fines in a single pass.
  • If your hotel is inside the old town, have them register your plate for your stay — a free pass that kills the whole risk.
  • Otherwise park outside and walk. Every historic center (Taormina, Cefalù, Catania) has one, and GPS happily routes you straight through it.

Local corners & granita

Off the tourist gauntlet

  • Palermo: hit the Ballarò or Capo street markets for pane con panelle, arancine, and sfincione at local prices — go mid-morning before the lunch crush, away from the tourist trattorias.
  • Granita, shaved to order. Real granita con brioche is a morning thing (9–11am): Pasticceria Savia in Catania and the historic cafés along Taormina’s Corso beat any resort’s pre-made tub.
  • Cascais tide pools for the kids. Praia das Avencas at low tide is a rock-pool playground of starfish, urchins, and anemones — a quiet, educational stop most visitors miss.
